ARABIC — TERMLY EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: ARABIC
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading Fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading Fluency.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Fluency.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Fluency.

2. When practising Speaking Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency.

3. When practising Extensive Reading: Library skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Extensive Reading: Library skills.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Extensive Reading: Library skills.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Extensive Reading: Library skills.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Extensive Reading: Library skills.

4. When practising Reading for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Information.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Information.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Information.

5. In ARABIC, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   B. Avoid speaking to classmates
   C. Mix random languages with no purpose
   D. Only memorise without using the language

6. When practising Intensive Reading: Poetry, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Poetry.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Poetry.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Poetry.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Poetry.

7. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.

8. When practising Listening Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening Comprehension.

9. When practising Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive Listening ● Scanning ● Vocabulary Building ● Extracting information.

10. When practising Selective Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Selective Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Selective Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Selective Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Selective Listening.

11. When practising Listening for Gist, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Gist.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Gist.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Gist.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Gist.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
12. In three clear sentences, explain Reading Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Information and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Intensive Reading: Poetry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Extensive Reading: Library skills and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Intensive Reading: Arabic Prose and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Handwriting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency.
